Subject: Sequencing MSA / DPA / Order Form — MAP & evaluation dependencies

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — things look promising. Procurement and legal here at Medico need to lock down sequencing for the MSA/DPA/order form before we can get final approval. A couple of constraints from our side:

- Security needs an SOC 2 attestation (or interim report) and a filled security questionnaire before legal will advance the MSA.
- Data residency notes must be explicit in the DPA (we host EHR-adjacent data in us-east only).
- Our procurement team requires the order form to reference the signed DPA and MSA and include the final pricing schedule and PO field.

Target: we are trying to have a pilot contract in place and initial provisioning by end of May (around 31 May). Can you share a mutual action plan (high level milestones & owners) and a proposed sequencing so we can run against our internal gating? Also: can we schedule a short (30m) sequencing call Monday 18 Apr?

Thanks — Alicia

Vanessa / Alicia — quick legal note on sequencing and a summary of DPA items we’ll need Medico to confirm:

1) Data processing scope — confirm the exact dataset classes (PHI adjacency noted by Alicia). We will map subprocessors and their locations.
2) Residency — we can contractually require processing in us-east for the pilot; want to understand if that must be permanent.
3) Indemnity & liability cap — propose a market-standard mutual cap, but if procurement insists on higher limits we’ll need C-suite approval.
4) KMS / key control — we support customer-managed keys via KMS; need to confirm whether Medico requires an HSM-backed offering.
5) SOC2 — we can provide our SOC2 Type II report and security questionnaire; will share by Apr 20 as Vanessa proposed.

Attaching: DPA_redlines_v1.docx with inline comments (sections: data residency, subprocessors, liability/indemnity).

If procurement cannot accept provisional provisioning prior to MSA signature, we should surface that to ops — we can do an engineering holdback (reduced access) to limit risk.

Subject: Re: Sequencing MSA / DPA / Order Form — MAP & evaluation dependencies

Vanessa / Rishi — thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifications and constraints from procurement/legal: 

- Procurement policy: we cannot issue any PO or start payment workflows until the MSA and DPA are both signed. We can, however, accept an order form that references the agreement and includes pricing so that we can prepare the PO once signatures are in place.
- Security: SOC2 attestation is required; please provide the report by Apr 20 so our security team can review before legal completes the MSA. If the SOC2 is delayed, legal will hold the MSA.
- Residency: for the pilot, us-east is fine, but we need a contractual path to restrict production to us-east or on-prem if the pilot expands.

Adjusted timeline (procurement view):
- Apr 18: Sequencing call (confirm)
- Apr 20: Security packet (SOC2 + questionnaire)
- Apr 22–May 6: Legal negotiation window (DPA redlines + MSA review)
- May 20: Target MSA/DPA sign (procurement to issue PO after signatures)
- May 31: Target start of pilot provisioning (ops to provision once PO accepted)

I’m attaching Medico_procurement_intake.pdf with our internal fields filled (billing code, PO owner, SOW acceptance checklist).

If you can update the MAP to show the legal gating points and the acceptance criteria Marcus will put together, procurement will queue the PO as soon as MSA/DPA are signed.

Alicia

Subject: Re: Sequencing MSA / DPA / Order Form — MAP & evaluation dependencies

Alicia — thanks, that helps. After talking to Rishi and ops we have an updated approach that should keep your procurement process happy while preserving the May 31 start target. Summary of updates: 

- We will deliver SOC2 Type II report and completed security questionnaire by Apr 20 (Maya will share).
- Rishi will push a constrained DPA redline set that locks residency for the pilot to us-east; broader residency language can be scoped for production.
- We will update the order form to include the pricing schedule and a PO field — procurement can fill and hold the PO until signatures are in place.
- Provisioning option: we can provision a sandbox/pilot environment for evaluation on May 31 under a provisional provisioning clause in the order form that requires the counter-signed MSA within 14 days of provisioning. If the MSA is not signed within 14 days, Redwood will suspend access until signatures are complete. This preserves your procurement rule (PO after MSA/DPA) while allowing a time-boxed pilot.

Attachments: updated MAP (redwood_MAP_v1.pdf — annotated), OrderForm_v1.xlsx (with provisional clause), DPA_redlines_v1.docx (cleaned comments).

Next steps / owners:
- Vanessa: schedule 18 Apr sequencing call (calendar invite sent)
- Maya: deliver SOC2 + questionnaire by Apr 20
- Rishi: submit DPA redlines by Apr 22
- Marcus: share pilot acceptance criteria by Apr 19
- Alicia / Medico procurement: confirm internal PO holder and billing code (per intake form)

If Proc still needs MSA sign before any provisioning, let us know and we’ll move provisioning to post-signature — the MAP will just shift MSA -> May 20 and provisioning -> 7 days after PO. Either way, we’re aligned on the gating items.

Thanks — looking forward to the call,
